analysis.title: Teradyne Inc. (TER): Solid quarter, with 2027 poised to sustain topline momentum - Buy
key_insights: GS expects TER to be range bound after a quarter and guidance just above the Street, against optimistic investor expectations built on GPU share gains, CPO TAM expansion in 2027, memory demand and robotics momentum.
Management expects 1Q27 revenue to grow sequentially from 4Q26, with sequential growth in each quarter of 2027, which contrasts with investor concern about softer 1H27 trends.
GS stays Buy on TER on sustained strength in VIP compute (ASIC programs) and memory (especially HBM/DRAM), plus the design win with a merchant GPU customer.
3Q26 revenue was $1.31bn versus GS $1.30bn and Street $1.27bn. Gross margin was 59.1% versus GS 59.0% and Street 58.6%. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.29 versus GS $2.15 and Street $2.05.

Segment results: Semi Test revenue $1.07bn was in line with GS $1.09bn and Street $1.05bn. Product Test revenue of $138mn was well above GS $110mn and Street $109mn. Robotics revenue of $96mn was below GS $105mn and Street $106mn.

Drivers of 2027 growth named by management: HBM-led memory growth from new fab capacity, improving compute demand as key ASIC programs ramp, and expanding opportunities in networking and product test. Two hyperscaler customers are expected to ramp from mid-2027, with a merchant GPU customer adding revenue.

Memory had a record quarter at $301mn, up 42% QoQ, on HBM and DRAM test demand and a NAND resurgence. Management expects strength to continue into 4Q and significant memory growth in 2027 as new fab capacity comes online.

Lower HBM stack heights are an incremental tailwind: constrained DRAM wafer supply can support more HBM stacks, which raises performance test demand. TER has higher share in HBM performance test than in DRAM wafer sort.
Robotics revenue was $96mn, down 4% QoQ. Growth is expected to resume in 4Q and continue in 2027, weighted to 2H, with revenue at its largest customer having tripled from 2025 to 2026.

Gross margin rose 60bps YoY to 59.1%. 4Q is guided to 58.0% at the midpoint, up 80bps YoY. Volume and mix, including accretive product test growth, are 2027 tailwinds, partly offset by input cost pressure.
4Q26 revenue guidance midpoint is $1.30bn, in line with GS and slightly above the Street at $1.28bn. Non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.95-$2.25 (midpoint $2.10) is above GS $2.03 and Street $2.05.

GS raises CY26-28 non-GAAP EPS estimates by an average of 7% on higher revenue and margin assumptions. The 12-month price target moves to $440 from $465 on a 35x P/E, down from 37x because of lower peer multiples, applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $12.50.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $440 from $465 on a lower peer-based multiple of 35x versus 37x, applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $12.50. Buy rating kept on VIP compute, HBM/DRAM memory and a merchant GPU design win.

earnings_insights: TER 3Q26 reported 10/28: revenue $1.306bn versus GS est $1.300bn and Street est $1.268bn. Non-GAAP EPS reported $2.29 versus GS est $2.15 and Street est $2.05.
TER 3Q26 reported gross margin 59.1% versus GS est 59.0% and Street est 58.6%. Reported operating margin 31.6% versus GS est 30.1% and Street est 29.8%.

TER 4Q26 guidance: revenue $1.25-1.35bn (midpoint $1.30bn) versus GS est $1.297bn and Street est $1.277bn. Non-GAAP EPS guidance $1.95-$2.25 (midpoint $2.10) versus GS est $2.03 and Street est $2.05. Gross margin guided to 58.0% at the midpoint versus Street est 58.5%.

GS non-GAAP EPS estimates (new vs old): 2026E $9.55 vs $9.20, 2027E $12.50 vs $11.50, 2028E $15.50 vs $14.25. Revenue estimates: 2026E $5,268mn vs $5,209mn, 2027E $6,499mn vs $6,229mn, 2028E $7,503mn vs $7,210mn.
Memory revenue was a record $301mn in 3Q26, up 42% QoQ. Robotics revenue was $96mn, down 4% QoQ.
risk_factors: Delays in the revenue ramp with a merchant GPU customer.
Significant quarterly volatility from the lumpy nature of large AI-related infrastructure projects.
Input cost pressures partly offsetting 2027 volume and mix gains in gross margin.
vol_and_positioning: GS says investor positioning into the quarter was moderately optimistic, despite a recent sector-wide selloff, given potential GPU share gains, CPO TAM expansion in 2027, memory demand and robotics momentum.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects sequential revenue growth in each quarter of 2027, backed by a strong exit backlog, HBM-led memory growth from new fab capacity, ASIC program ramps, two hyperscaler customers ramping from mid-2027 and a merchant GPU customer.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors had worried about softer 1H27 trends. GS also expects the stock to be range bound because guidance was only just above the Street against optimistic expectations. Risks include lumpy AI infrastructure projects and delays in the merchant GPU ramp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delays in the revenue ramp with a merchant GPU customer.

theme_stances.key_argument: Sustained strength in VIP compute (ASIC programs) and memory, especially HBM/DRAM, plus a merchant GPU design win, should drive further revenue upside in 2027 and beyond.
